(2) User-confirmed DB design (D2 + D7): role jbh_monitor LOGIN, GRANT pg_monitor, pg_stat_statements in db postgres, -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c pg_stat_statements.track=top in compose.local.yaml only; initdb/02 skips with exit 0 when JBH_PG_MONITOR_PASSWORD empty, password passed via psql :'pw'. (3) compose.local.yaml jbh-alloy: grafana/alloy:v1.22.0, user 473:473, ports only on 127.0.0.1 (14317,14318,12347,12345), no Docker socket, healthcheck /-/ready, DSN nested default+override. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT/OTEL_SDK_DISABLED/JBH_ENV names exact on 4 Docker backends. (4) Alloy: header comment in every file (what, who imports, env vars); no secret in a file; D3 remote_write, D5 transform, D6 honor_labels, D15 faro.receiver; module args reusable by a later prod.alloy. (5) Docs: LOCAL.md SQL for existing volume, Mac Postgres, IDE settings; README local paragraph only; observability/README Tech stack kept; design.md 'Moved to JBH-84' section kept in full. Signals: all assistant-run by the leader (assistantRunsTests): compose config -q both files exit 0, V9-V14, V17, guard run exit 0, alloy validate local + modules + combined wiring exit 0 with failing negative controls. findings.note: compose.local.yaml:204-227 (service jbh-alloy): no healthcheck. Spec alloy-deploy 'Local Alloy publishes on loopback only' requires a healthcheck on /-/ready; design.md D2 gives the bash /dev/tcp healthcheck text; V9 and the brief expect it. Leader's V9 pass claim does not match the committed file (grep '/-/ready' compose.local.yaml finds nothing). Add the D2 healthcheck block (or the spec and design must be changed with a user-visible decision).

compose.local.yaml jbh-alloy: no memory limit. otlp.alloy memory_limiter uses limit_percentage (percent of the container limit), so with no limit it has no useful ceiling. JBH-55 plan section 1 asks for a memory limit; design D11 says no hardening block. Add a mem_limit/deploy limit (for example 256M) or state in the otlp.alloy comment that the percentage is of host memory locally.
